title: Certified Optimal Intervals in the Critical Current-Status and Right-Censored Experiment
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the delivered result incremental below the field floor (paper_score_ceiling 6.3 < 7.4; salvageable=false); the math REVISE flags only a redundant baseline-continuity assumption, as independently adjudicated from the completed D0 proof record.
gap_reasons: It does not determine the gain elbow or establish any gain at κ=1, and the framing correctly leaves that endpoint open rather than presenting a complete source-allocation frontier.

The certificate construction proves termination but offers no tractability guarantee or executed numerical frontier, while original-data validity requires known baselines and mechanisms, substantially limiting immediate practical use.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a uniform two-sided rational LP certificate, an oracle-known original-data transport, and a full-class strict mixed-source gain for κ in [327,1000], with L_1000 ≤ 461/6250. D0.5 graded the sound result incremental below the field floor because the gain elbow and κ=1 case remain open, no executed or tractable frontier is supplied, and the transport uses known baseline mechanisms. The math panel also flagged a redundant standalone baseline-continuity assumption; its redundancy was independently verified, but D0.5 did not issue a mathematical pass and the archived dependency graph remains nonminimal.
tldr: This field-tier result is an oracle-known offline design-calibration theorem for the critical current-status and right-censored experiment. One rational refinement schedule defines, jointly for every \(\kappa\in[1,1000]\), a finite reconstructed experiment, outward rational probability rows, lower and upper connected-action programs, their exact values, and a uniform error budget; legal spline nets make the certificates converge uniformly to the full-class minimax expected length. Endpoint inflation and full-range repair yield an honest limit action, and an executable comparison kernel transports it to prospectively generated original records under the known baseline and mechanisms. The exact symbolic record \(\mathfrak C_{1000}\) now uses a rational weighted-Poisson estimator to certify a strict full-class mixed-source gain for every \(\kappa\in[327,1000]\), with the sharper endpoint bound \(L_{1000}\le461/6250\). Poisson thinning makes the gain set an upper interval, while whether its lower endpoint reaches \(\kappa=1\) remains open.
gap: The mixed-censor critical experiment has an abstract minimax interval value but no deterministic optimizer certificate. Generic finite confidence-game LPs do not jointly control an infinite tangent class, continuous Gaussian and Poisson observations, a moving scalar target, or uniform variation in the cohort intensity.
fill: A legal inner spline net and one common rational schedule produce \(\kappa\)-indexed finite experiments, probability enclosures, primal--dual programs, and explicit error budgets with a uniform vanishing gap. A positioning corollary separates that continuum certificate from exact-finite MES validation and fixed-fraction efficiency. Endpoint repair supplies honest actions, finite-coordinate kernels supply prospective original-data transport, and a complete rational endpoint record certifies a strict full-class gain at \(\kappa=1000\).
